title: Marguerite and the Hollow
premise: Lior Dunmore has survived two decades in the port city of Vell by tasting the king's food and selling harmless charms, hiding a gift that law and fear have driven underground. When the crown's witch-hunt sweeps up Lior's young apprentice, they are forced to seek the Hollow—a collapsed realm beneath the city where an ancient covenant between human and fae magic was shattered. To save their apprentice and every marked mage in Vell, Lior must reforge that covenant, but doing so demands surrendering the very power they've spent a lifetime concealing to someone who could corrupt it. In the end, Lior breaks the covenant open rather than reforging it alone, distributing its keeping among many hands so no crown—and no single heart—can ever own magic again.
about_author: Wendell Iversen is the pen name of a former line cook who spent eleven years in harbor-city kitchens before turning to fantasy. They write about people whose work is invisible until it becomes dangerous.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A routine morning: tasting the king's breakfast, dosing immunity tonics, slipping a luck-charm to a fishmonger's daughter. We learn the rules of survival in outlawed-magic Vell—never glow, never heal, never be seen twice. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A List of Names
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The crown posts the Registry Act: all gifted persons must declare or be hunted. Lior burns their own name from an old guild ledger while their apprentice, Sefa, watches with dangerous curiosity. Emotional beat: dread arriving as paperwork.

chapters.title: What Sefa Carried
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sixteen and reckless, Sefa uses a warming charm in public to save a freezing beggar child—and is seen. Watchmen come at dusk; Sefa flees through the fish market as Lior covers their escape. Emotional beat: guilt and fierce protectiveness colliding.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Sefa is taken anyway; the captain offers a trade—Lior's cooperation identifying other mages for the girl's release. Lior refuses and instead seeks Maren Ostwick, a disgraced archivist who knows where the Hollow opens. Emotional beat: choosing treason with open eyes.

chapters.title: Down the Drowned Stair
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lior and Maren descend through a flooded cistern into the Hollow, a twilight realm of petrified bargains and whispering stone. They find the covenant-shard, cracked for a century, and learn what mending it will cost. Emotional beat: awe curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Hollow Remembers
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Within the Hollow, Maren confronts her past—she helped break the covenant as a young court mage, believing she was protecting the realm. The shard shows her the corruption that followed. Emotional beat: confession as the beginning of repair.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Registry
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Above, the hunt turns brutal: mages burned in the granary square, and Lior's fellow taster executed as a suspected poisoner. Lior realizes the king isn't hunting danger—he's harvesting fear to fuel his claim on the covenant's power. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Imprisoned, Sefa is offered freedom if she'll swear her gift to the crown. She refuses, inspired by stories of Lior's refusal, and organizes the cell-block mages into quiet resistance. Emotional beat: courage inherited rather than found.

chapters.title: Climax: The Shattering Hour
chapters.summary: All three POVs converge. During the king's coronation-rite meant to seize the covenant whole, Lior shatters the binding ceremony from within the Hollow, offering their own gift as kindling—but instead of dying, they split the covenant's keeping into thousands of sparks that settle on every gifted person in Vell. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into distribution.

chapters.title: Many Hands
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, months later. Magic is legal again but owned by no one; Sefa teaches openly, Maren rebuilds the archive as a commons, and Lior still tastes the king's food—now as a citizen's check on power, not a servant's. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace with vigilance at its edges.
